_doc: Rival geneticists (ROADMAP §3.8). requiresNodes gates each rival on the conquest that puts their COUNTER-class anatomy in your reach — you are never asked to beat Air before wings exist for you too; requiresRivals chains the ladder. Rivals field CHIMERAS, not human units: campaign/rivals.js builds each rival's team from real parts and runs it through the same physiology the player uses (splice/physiology.js), so a rival's stats, tags and elemental class are earned by anatomy exactly like yours. classBias picks the anatomy they commit to; the ladder is ordered so each rival counters the class you just farmed off the last one (Ground → Air → Water → back to Ground), which is what makes keeping a stable better than perfecting one build. Beating a rival puts their chimeras in Containment; salvaging one yields THEIR parts — the roadmap's 'enemy tech is otherwise unobtainable', except here it is other people's genetics. Rivals iterate: every defeat raises their grade ladder and power, and counterBias lets them answer whatever class you field most. monologue follows the §3.8 schema (intro / midFight / defeat / victory / dissectionTaunt) — one-line barks now, prose later, no refactor. Balance pass: rivals were tuned against a lone chimera and folded against the team of three the game actually gives you — they were the EASIEST content on the ladder. powerScale/teamSize/grades now put them at the top of it, with the class triangle deciding: bring the counter and you win ~90%, mirror ~40-65%, bring what they counter and you lose.

rivals.name: Dr. Mantissa
rivals.title: Chief Entomologist, Hexapod Futures
rivals.philosophy: Six legs. Always six legs. Anything fewer is sentimentality.

monologue.intro: Ah — the goat person. I have read your paperwork. It is atrocious. My arthropods will explain why.
monologue.midFight: You are improvising. I ANNOTATED. There is a difference and it is about to become obvious.
monologue.defeat: Fine! FINE. Take my specimens. They were a rough draft anyway. The next instar will be less polite.
monologue.victory: Peer review complete. Findings: you need more legs. Considerably more legs.
monologue.dissectionTaunt: Your creature is in my lab. It has been given a name tag and a very small chair.

rivals.name: Baroness Vesper Aloft
rivals.title: Aloft Aeronautical Genetics, Chair of Everything
rivals.philosophy: Legs are luggage. I have simply stopped packing them.

monologue.intro: How lovely. You brought things that touch the ground. I brought things that decline to.
monologue.midFight: You keep swinging at where I was. It is charming. It is also the whole problem.
monologue.defeat: Grounded. Me. GROUNDED. Keep the wings — I have blueprints and an unhealthy amount of free time.
monologue.victory: Do give my regards to the horizon. You will be looking at it for some time.
monologue.dissectionTaunt: Your creature is up here with me now. The view is spectacular. The paperwork is not.

rivals.name: Professor Abyssa Trench
rivals.title: Director, Marianas Applied Wetworks
rivals.philosophy: Pressure is just the universe insisting on rigor.

monologue.intro: Eleven kilometres down, nothing hurries and nothing forgives. I brought some of it with me.
monologue.midFight: You are running out of air. Metaphorically. For now.
monologue.defeat: Extraordinary. Wholly unreplicated, of course. Bring your notebook next time — I intend to iterate.
monologue.victory: The pressure differential did most of the work. I merely stood here being correct.
monologue.dissectionTaunt: Your creature is in a tank. It is being observed. It is, in fairness, being fed.
